Whether wider per-thread work improves full-call time while meeting the FP64 error bound remains for controller measurement.

More independent accumulators were not faster in these trials, motivating a contrasting test of contiguous pair loads and CTA mapping rather than simply increasing accumulator count.

model_interpretation.claim: Compared with the measured 256-thread, four-accumulator fused mapping, 128-thread CTAs can retain the same 256-float tile boundaries by assigning two adjacent floats to each lane. An aligned float2 path may reduce load instruction overhead, while a scalar fallback preserves correctness for 4-byte-aligned inputs and an explicit odd-element path handles tails. Keeping 1024 CTAs/partials and the 256-thread finalizer fixed makes this a contrasting within-CTA mapping experiment; its effect on full-call time and the FP64 error bound remains for controller measurement.

items.subject: Within-CTA streaming and reduction mapping
items.objective: Use the two-stage fused topology as a controlled starting point. Hold global input tile boundaries, partial count, and finalizer organization fixed for each comparison; explore within-CTA streaming and reduction mapping, including multiple accumulators, suitable contiguous/vector loads, and CTA dimensions or work per thread. Handle alignment and tails for every valid input. Do not retune global partitioning or finalizer fan-in, which T1 owns. Validate all required sizes and the stated FP64 error bound, and measure full-call time.
